title: Reddit CEO Declares ‘People Don’t Want AI Summaries—They Want Reddit’
excerpt: Reddit, Inc. stock fell nearly 10% in Friday’s premarket session after investors focused on management’s warning that search referral traffic remained “chopp...
content_html:
Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.

Reddit, Inc. stock fell nearly 10% in Friday's premarket session after investors focused on management's warning that search referral traffic remained "choppy" amid ongoing uncertainty around Google's AI-driven search changes, overshadowing another quarter of better-than-expected revenue and earnings.

CEO Steve Huffman said search referrals were "choppy" during the second quarter and became more volatile later in the period as Google's AI-powered search continues to evolve.

He said Reddit is prioritizing direct engagement through its app over search-driven traffic, adding that the company is "not building for drive-by traffic" but rather "a daily destination" and that direct app users are significantly more valuable than search referrals.

Earnings Snapshot

Reddit reported second-quarter earnings of $1.25 per share, beating the analyst consensus estimate of 95 cents, according to Benzinga Pro.

Revenue increased 61% year over year to $804.9 million, topping the Street estimate of $730.3 million. The quarter marked Reddit's eighth consecutive period of revenue growth exceeding 60%.

Management said advertising demand remained strong across sales channels, particularly among large enterprise customers.

Advertising revenue climbed 64% year over year to $762 million, while other revenue increased 24% to $43 million. Active advertisers rose more than 70% from a year earlier, led by strength in the retail and travel categories.

Ads API revenue grew more than 40% sequentially, while more than half of revenue came from credit-line customer relationships.

Revenue from dynamic product ads and app install campaigns more than doubled from a year earlier. Scaled channel revenue from mid-market and small- and medium-sized business advertisers also doubled.

Trending: Avoid the #1 Investing Mistake: How Your 'Safe' Holdings Could Be Costing You Big Time

Gross margin expanded 50 basis points year over year to 91.3%, despite higher artificial intelligence and machine learning computing costs. Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 43%, with third-quarter guidance implying a midpoint margin of 45%.

Operating cash flow more than doubled to $262 million, while trailing 12-month operating cash flow surpassed $1 billion for the first time.

Reddit, Inc. 股价在周五盘前交易中下跌近 10%，此前投资者关注的是管理层的警告，即由于谷歌人工智能驱动的搜索变化持续存在不确定性，搜索推荐流量仍然“不稳定”，掩盖了又一个季度好于预期的收入和收益。

首席执行官史蒂夫·霍夫曼表示，第二季度搜索推荐量“不稳定”，随着谷歌人工智能搜索的不断发展，搜索推荐量在该季度后期变得更加不稳定。

他表示，Reddit 优先考虑通过其应用程序进行直接参与，而不是搜索驱动的流量，并补充说，该公司“不是为路过式流量而构建”，而是“为日常目的地”，并且直接应用程序用户比搜索推荐更有价值。

盈利概况

根据 Benzinga Pro 的数据，Reddit 报告第二季度每股收益为 1.25 美元，超过分析师普遍预期的 95 美分。

收入同比增长 61% 至 8.049 亿美元，高于华尔街预期的 7.303 亿美元。 该季度标志着 Reddit 连续第八个季度收入增长超过 60%。

管理层表示，整个销售渠道的广告需求依然强劲，尤其是大型企业客户。

广告收入同比增长 64% 至 7.62 亿美元，其他收入增长 24% 至 4300 万美元。 在零售和旅游类别的强劲带动下，活跃广告客户同比增长超过 70%。

广告 API 收入环比增长超过 40%，其中一半以上的收入来自信用额度客户关系。

动态产品广告和应用安装活动的收入比一年前增长了一倍多。 来自中端市场和中小型企业广告商的规模化渠道收入也翻了一番。

趋势：避免第一大投资错误：你的“安全”持仓可能会让你付出巨大的代价

尽管人工智能和机器学习计算成本较高，但毛利率仍同比增长 50 个基点至 91.3%。 调整后 EBITDA 利润率达到 43%，第三季度指导意味着中点利润率为 45%。

运营现金流增加了一倍多，达到 2.62 亿美元，而过去 12 个月的运营现金流首次超过 10 亿美元。
